tagline: Crozet's toll road over the Alleghenies, and the war over it.
intro: From Parkersburg on the Ohio the old turnpike follows the Little Kanawha into the hills on WV 47, takes US 33 through Weston and Buckhannon to Elkins, then US 250 up the Tygart Valley through Beverly and Huttonsville. From there it climbs over Cheat Mountain and comes down to Bartow on the East Fork of the Greenbrier.

Claudius Crozet, who had served under Napoleon, laid it out for Virginia, under orders that it nowhere exceed a grade of four degrees. In 1861 both armies wanted it. At Rich Mountain a local boy led a Union brigade through the woods to the rear of the Confederate line, for a promised hundred dollars in gold.

moments.title: Beverly
moments.text: The oldest settlement in the Tygart Valley kept the county seat for more than a century, until Elkins took it in 1899 after an intense local political war.

moments.title: Cheat Summit Fort
moments.text: The highest Union camp of the war watched the turnpike from 4,085 feet. Snow came on August 13, horses froze in September, and the fort was given up the next April.

moments.title: Camp Allegheny
moments.text: Confederates held the pass at about 4,400 feet through a bitter winter, and the December 1861 fight here kept Highland County in Virginia.

practical: Rich Mountain, Cheat Mountain and Camp Allegheny are reached by state-designated backways, which are unpaved or have only short paved stretches.
